Theophylline kinetic studies, serial spirometric function tests, and arterial blood gas determinations were performed in 39 adult men with stable chronic obstructive airway disease (COPD). Subjects were given an intravenous aminophylline loading dose of 5.6 mg/kg and a maintenance dose of 0.9 mg/kg/hr for 6 hours. Elderly (greater than 60 years old) nonsmoking subjects had 36% lower theophylline clearance (Cl) and a 40% longer serum theophylline elimination t1/2 than did middle-aged (less than 60 years old) nonsmoking subjects (mean +/- SE; clearances of 32.6 +/- 3.2 [n = 13] and 50.7 +/- 8.5 ml/kg/hr [n = 8] and t1/2s of 11.0 +/- 0.8 and 7.4 +/- 0.8 hours, respectively).
